question: How much faster, smaller and lighter is answering the EUDR screen/decision question from the decision layers than from the original layers, and which lever (representation, selection, registry, table) contributes what?

environment.compression: Python standard-library compression.zstd; codec defines settings

method.hot: per run, `hot_rounds` (2) fresh children per path, run in opposite path order so no path is always first or last; in each, imports and the single load happen first, then warmups, then N measured batches per workload. Wall is perf_counter_ns around the whole batch. CPU is the main thread (thread_time_ns, 42 ns resolution; the process clock is 1 microsecond on macOS, too coarse for table batches). The batch answer digest is checked outside the timer after every batch. Load time is excluded as in the retained harness.
method.process_cold: retained definition: fresh Python child per repetition, timed full load + one 17-plot batch AFTER imports and geometry read. Everything a lazy import would pull in at first call is imported before the timer. Repetitions are interleaved across paths and rotated, so machine drift hits every path alike. The OS file cache is uncontrolled and warm; this is not disk-cold.
method.end_to_end: parent-measured wall of a fresh `python -B -m engine.decision_benchmark --e2e <path>` that reads the request (plot IDs and hashes, or geometries) on stdin, imports only what the path needs, loads, answers the 17 registered plots and prints the answer digest. Includes interpreter start-up, imports, the stdin parse and process exit. Two floors are measured the same way: `python -B -c pass` and the harness no-op (module import + request parse); the net columns subtract them. Engine bytecode caches are pre-built and read.
method.memory: peak RSS is the child lifetime high-water mark (retained rss_record) taken from the process-cold and end-to-end children; "held" is the loaded arrays' nbytes; "traced" is Python/numpy allocation after load from tracemalloc (GDAL C buffers are not seen) in a separate untimed child. The traced peak counts requested allocations, including calloc pages never touched, so it can exceed the resident peak; RSS is the resident figure.
method.storage: bytes of the files each path opens, read with stat() from the files in this checkout (provenance and JRC side files included for the original paths); geometry and supplier inputs are common and excluded.
method.p95: nearest rank (engine.benchmark.summarize); hot batches pool all runs, so p95 is the 95th of the pooled batches
method.pooling: the whole benchmark runs `runs` times back to back in this one parent; every child is a fresh process. The headline median and p95 pool the samples of all runs; per-run medians and the spread between them are reported.
method.binding: before timing, the parent recomputes every path in-process and requires equality: original vs screen store vs decision store vs fast selection vs the one-call batch evaluator on W1, W3 and W4, and the registry, the numpy-free lite re-check and the table against the proof outputs on W1. Every timed child returns an answer digest that must equal the pinned one, or nothing is published. W1 expected outputs are proof-v1.json's; P0 is checked against engine.query.evaluate and the retained benchmark-v1.json digest.
method.thread_limits: children run with OMP, OpenBLAS, MKL and VECLIB threads set to 1; sequential, never in parallel

limitations: P0 answers a bigger question than P1-P6: it returns the 101-bin canopy histogram and the full lossyear histogram. P1 is the apples-to-apples original-layers baseline for the contract question.

P5L (decision_lite) binds the store level and grid once at load and keeps each plot's decoded codes; it does not check the header's decoded-raster hash (the request supplies the pinned store sha256 instead). It reads only split-encoded stores.
The registry and the table exist only for registered plots. A plot that is new or whose geometry changed has no entry and takes the P3/P4 path.

P4B answers a whole batch in one call, so it needs the batch in hand: a single new plot gains nothing (below decision_batch.MIN_BATCH = 4 it just runs the P4 loop), and the 17-plot W1 batch is small, so the roughly 100 us fixed per-call cost of its numpy passes is spread over few plots. Its per-plot figures are batch time / items; the gain is larger on the 500-plot W3 batch.
Fast selection is exact (fuzz-equal to select_cells) but faster only on ordinary plot shapes; on boundary-heavy adversarial polygons (W4) it can be slower, because many centres go to exact GEOS.
The OS file cache is warm and uncontrolled: nothing here is disk-cold, object-store or network latency.
One Apple M5 laptop, other processes running, AC power. Medians and p95 are reported with the spread between two runs; differences under that spread are not findings.
Small AOI: a 1233 x 604 cell chip (744,732 cells) and 17 real plots. Whole-tile or global behaviour is not measured here.
W3 is synthetic: seeded random concave polygons, not company data; its shapes and land placement are assumptions.
The table path takes the layer version (store sha256) from the request. Verifying it by hashing the store file costs the file read and a sha256 (side_measurements) and is not in the table timings.
End-to-end numbers assume engine bytecode caches exist. Without them each module is compiled at start-up (side_measurements.uncached_compile_ms), which would hit the larger new modules hardest.
Outputs are mapped observations, never legal compliance findings.

W3.generator:
Seeded plot-like polygons: synthetic, not company data.

Star-shaped about an interior point (sorted angles with gaps under 0.9 pi, radii 0.35-1 of the
unit), then stretched 1-2.2x and rotated: concave, elongated, valid. About 15% carry a hole
(the shell scaled by 0.3). Net area is log-uniform in 0.5-20 ha, measured with local
metres-per-degree. Centres sit on land cells of the screen layer; polygons stay inside the chip.

W4.what: adversarial boundary-stressing polygons from the test fuzz generator (aligned edges, vertices on cell centres, ulp offsets, slivers, lattices); P3, P4 and P4B only
